input._script:
using CUDA
using JSON3

# The backend must be CUDA. JACC 1.3.1 reads its backend from Preferences,
# not from the environment, so an ENV variable here would do nothing. A
# JACC run on the threads backend returns the same numbers as a run on the
# GPU, so the numbers alone cannot tell the two apart. This check compares
# the array type instead, which differs.
#
# Set the preference once, on the login node, in the default environment
# and with no project flag:
#   julia -e 'import JACC; JACC.set_backend(:cuda)'
# Preferences are read when a package loads, so the change takes effect on
# the next job.
function jacc_backend_info()
    d = Dict{String,Any}()
    d["array_type"] = try string(JACC.array_type()) catch e; "unavailable" end
    d["backend"]    = try string(JACC.default_backend()) catch e; "unavailable" end
    at = try string(typeof(JACC.array(Float32[1, 2]))) catch e; "unavailable" end
    d["sample_array_type"] = at
    # "unavailable" means the accessor threw. That is a failure, not a
    # device array, so it must not read as on_device.
    d["on_device"] = at != "unavailable" && !startswith(at, "Vector") && !startswith(at, "Array")
    return d
end

function jacc_vadd_i(i, y, a, b)
    y[i] = a[i] + b[i]
end

result = Dict{String,Any}()

# Node identity and CUDA versions, recorded before any kernel launch.
# A SIGSEGV inside cuModuleLoadDataEx killed the multi-GPU a30 check on
# 2026-09-05 and passed on retry. The crash is not catchable, so the
# result JSON is lost and the node stays unknown. These fields go into
# the Slurm log instead, which survives the crash, and into the result
# when the job completes. A driver older than the runtime is the first
# thing to check for a module-load fault.
node_info = Dict{String,Any}("hostname" => gethostname())
try
    node_info["driver"]  = string(CUDA.driver_version())
    node_info["runtime"] = string(CUDA.runtime_version())
catch e
    node_info["versions_error"] = sprint(showerror, e)
end
println(stderr, "NODE: ", node_info)
flush(stderr)

result["node"] = node_info
input = JSON3.read(ARGS[1])
a_host = Float32.(input.a)
b_host = Float32.(input.b)
n = length(a_host)

# --- raw CUDA.jl ---
try
    if !CUDA.functional()
        result["cuda"] = Dict("error" => "CUDA is not functional on this node")
    else
        function vadd_kernel!(y, a, b)
            i = (blockIdx().x - 1) * blockDim().x + threadIdx().x
            if i <= length(y)
                @inbounds y[i] = a[i] + b[i]
            end
            return nothing
        end
        a_dev = CuArray(a_host)
        b_dev = CuArray(b_host)
        y_dev = CUDA.zeros(Float32, n)
        threads = 256
        blocks = cld(n, threads)
        @cuda threads=threads blocks=blocks vadd_kernel!(y_dev, a_dev, b_dev)
        CUDA.synchronize()
        result["cuda"] = Dict("result" => Array(y_dev), "device" => CUDA.name(CUDA.device()))
    end
catch e
    result["cuda"] = Dict("error" => sprint(showerror, e))
end

# --- JACC.jl ---
# The import stays in its own completed top-level statement. Julia
# macro-expands a whole top-level block before it runs any of it, so an
# import cannot share a block with code that uses a macro from the
# package it imports.
try
    import JACC
catch e
    result["jacc"] = Dict("error" => "import JACC failed: $(sprint(showerror, e))")
end
if !haskey(result, "jacc")
    try
        a_j = JACC.array(a_host)
        b_j = JACC.array(b_host)
        y_j = JACC.zeros(Float32, n)
        # JACC.parallel_for(dims, f, x...) calls f(i, x...) per index.
        # f must be a named function -- confirmed via methods(JACC.parallel_for)
        # on 2026-09-05; JACC's macro form and JACC.Array do not exist as
        # this health check originally assumed.
        JACC.parallel_for(n, jacc_vadd_i, y_j, a_j, b_j)
        JACC.synchronize()
        info = jacc_backend_info()
        info["result"] = Array(y_j)
        if !info["on_device"]
            info["error"] = "JACC ran on the host. array_type is $(info["sample_array_type"]). " *
                            "Run `julia -e 'import JACC; JACC.set_backend(:cuda)'` once on the " *
                            "login node, in the default environment, with no project flag. " *
                            "A JACC result computed on the host says nothing about the GPU."
        end
        result["jacc"] = info
    catch e
        result["jacc"] = Dict("error" => sprint(showerror, e))
    end
end

println(JSON3.write(result))
